title: Tokens and Training
summary: Long prompts mean more time and cost — shorten them before switching models.

sections.heading: Orientation — Lesson Start
sections.subtitle: Lesson Start
sections.contentMarkdown:
- What will you understand? Why do long prompts take more time and cost more — and how does this affect every prompt you write?
- Why now? When you build an AI feature in your product — every character counts. Shortening is not a luxury — it’s design.
- What after the lesson? You will compare a short prompt and a long prompt and identify what to remove.

sections.heading: Tension — Long Prompt — Slow or Expensive Response
sections.subtitle: Long Prompt — Slow or Expensive Response
sections.contentMarkdown:
- You wrote a long introduction and said, "please" and "my friend" — and the response came after a while, or the API bill increased.
- It doesn’t necessarily mean the model is "slow" — often you sent too much text.
- In Lovable or Cursor: the larger the context — the slower the processing and response. Rule: Shorten — you gain.

sections.heading: Core Idea — Long Inputs and Outputs = More Time and Cost
sections.subtitle: Long Inputs and Outputs = More Time and Cost
sections.contentMarkdown:
- AI breaks your text into small pieces (tokens) — a token = a word or a part of it.
- Every token in input and every token in response counts: speed, cost, memory limit.
- When you build: a long system prompt + user context + conversation history = bill and time. Shorten what is not necessary.
- Shorten the prompt, define what is needed, remove introductions — often the same result at a lower cost.

sections.heading: Comparison — Same Prompt · Two Phrasings
sections.subtitle: Same Prompt · Two Phrasings
sections.contentMarkdown:
| Fluff and Introductions | Direct |
|-------------|--------|
| "My AI friend, please can you help me with a simple task, which is to summarize this article..." — the entire introduction is a waste of tokens | "Summarize the article in 3 points." — a short sentence, faster response, lower cost, and the same result |

sections.heading: Glossary — Two Terms to Start
sections.subtitle: Two Terms to Start
sections.contentMarkdown:
| Term | Meaning | Example |
|---------|--------|------|
| Token | A small piece of text — a word or a part of it. AI counts it in and out | "Hello" can be one token or two depending on language and model |
| Training | The stage before you use the model — it learns from a huge amount of texts. You do not train it; you just use it | ChatGPT is trained on internet texts — you just write a prompt |

sections.heading: Diagram Block (Intent)
sections.contentMarkdown: From prompt to response — every step counts (ID: `ai-summarization-flow`): Prompt → Tokenization → Model → Response Every step in the process consumes tokens. When you shorten the prompt — you shorten the entire process.

sections.heading: Quiz — Quick Check
sections.subtitle: Quick Check
sections.contentMarkdown:
Question: If AI is slow to respond — what is the first thing you try?
Change the model immediately.
Shorten your prompt and remove excess introductions.
Wait and try again without changes.
Explanation: Shortening the prompt is the fastest improvement — before changing tools or models.
bullets: Shorten your prompt and remove excess introductions.

sections.heading: Mission — Short vs Long Prompt — What Will You Remove?
sections.subtitle: Short vs Long Prompt — What Will You Remove?
sections.contentMarkdown:
The task: Same prompt in two phrasings: one long and one short. 10 minutes is enough. Delivery: 1. The long prompt (write or copy it)
2. The short prompt (same request, fewer words)
3. What did you remove from the long one? (Introductions, repetition, extra details)
4. If the feature in your product will run 100 times/day — what will shortening save you? Evaluation Criteria: | Dimension | Weight | Criteria |
|-------|-------|---------|
| Real Comparison | 60% | Both prompts for the same request; the short one is actually shorter |
| Shortening Analysis | 40% | Identified what was removed and why; linked to cost or speed in the product |
